content: WordPress block themes (theme.json) define a bounded color palette, font families, spacing scale under 'settings', consumed as CSS custom properties on the body. Since WP 6.6, themes can ship multiple 'style variations' (JSON files in /styles) that only override the palette/typography tokens — user picks one in the Site Editor, and the CSS variables update site-wide without touching block markup. WooCommerce as of 2026 is still transitioning to block themes for checkout/product layouts; classic PHP themes remain common for heavy customization, which is closer to Voltique's 'never per-theme markup' constraint than legacy WooCommerce Customizer (which allowed arbitrary CSS injection).
